axes.question: Can the target users accomplish their task efficiently and without confusion — is the flow learnable, are affordances and states clear, is error recovery forgiving?
Does this cohere with the established design system, platform conventions, and the product's existing patterns — or introduce a one-off that fragments the experience?
Does this move the user toward the intended action — is the primary call-to-action clear, the path low-friction, the value legible at the decision point?
Is this something users will want to use — does it feel polished, trustworthy, and appropriate for the brand and audience?
Is the content clear, scannable, and correctly leveled for the audience — labels, microcopy, information hierarchy, and reading order?
Can this be built and maintained within the frontend-stack, component-library, and effort constraints — reusing existing components rather than demanding new infrastructure?

Does this meet accessibility requirements — perceivable, operable, understandable for users with disabilities (contrast, semantic structure, keyboard, visible focus, target size)? A hard WCAG A/AA barrier is a VETO gate, not a tradeoff — candidate-level only (ADR-0042 Non-Goal 6): runtime testing of focus order, keyboard traversal, and screen-reader behavior is required to certify conformance.

investigate.next_action: <compact selected_next + why + next_command — e.g. Frame the UX problem from this cited brief (/designer:frame)>

frame.next_action: Decide on a design direction given this frame (/designer:decide)

artifact: <table or list of directions with tradeoffs across the resolved design axes>
<chosen direction + rationale + accessibility gate verdict + risks>
decide.rationale_gate: decisive 사용성/archetype axis + the accessibility gate verdict
decide.next_action: Compose the flows/specs for the chosen direction (/designer:compose)

artifact: <the design artifact: IA / flow (with per-screen state set) / wireframe
structure / component specs / CTA copy — every element annotated with its
accessibility + consistency acceptance criteria, [to be validated] markers
compose.rationale_gate: how the artifact honors the confirmed frame + chosen direction, plus its accessibility + consistency acceptance criteria
compose.evidence_pointers: spec sections / flow states / brief path
compose.next_action: Critique the composed design spec, and the rendered screen once built (/designer:critique)

artifact: Gate verdict: 접근성 Accessibility [PASS/CONDITIONAL/FAIL] (candidate-level; focus-order / keyboard / screen-reader unverified — runtime)
<severity-grouped findings: CRITICAL / MAJOR / MINOR / SUGGESTION, each
[element/region] [lens] — [finding + failure signal + criteria ref]; plus Looks Strong>
critique.rationale_gate: the decisive findings + the accessibility gate verdict
critique.evidence_pointers: finding sections / criteria refs / artifact path
critique.next_action: <compact selected_next + why + next_command — e.g. Address CRITICAL/MAJOR findings (/designer:refine), or proceed to commit when nothing blocks and the gate is not FAIL>

artifact: - Verified: <downstream elements reconcile; accessibility gate exposure
unchanged; measurable success metrics intact; [to be validated] markers intact>
- Render status (post-code only): <re-rendered screen read host-direct | re-render unavailable / broke — vision re-critique UNVERIFIED | N/A (pre-code)>

- Re-critique: <converged — no new CRITICAL/MAJOR + accessibility gate not FAIL (PASS, or CONDITIONAL with named preconditions) | NOT converged — new findings / regression / gate FAIL / vision UNVERIFIED>
- Convergence: <CONVERGED | PAUSED — bounded passes exhausted / regression / render unavailable → routed to owner decision | /designer:decide | /designer:investigate>
refine.rationale_gate: the design reconciles + the accessibility gate verdict
refine.evidence_pointers: revised elements / criteria refs / artifact path
refine.next_action: <compact selected_next + why + next_command — e.g. Re-critique the revised artifact to confirm convergence (/designer:critique), or proceed to commit when converged and the gate is not FAIL>

start.next_action: Hand the spec to the frontend (/engineer:start or /orchestrator:plan); optionally /designer:start the next surface

peer.privacy_scope: proprietary UI, unreleased features/flows, customer data visible in screenshots, and secret-bearing frontend code
